root_cause.text: perf’s sched/callchain code used only `current->flags & (PF_KTHREAD | PF_USER_WORKER)` to decide whether it was safe to access user-space state, but a task can still have those flags while its `mm` has already been freed during exit, leading to a NULL-pointer dereference when perf reads `task->mm`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `is_user_task(struct task_struct *task) { return task->mm && !(task->flags & (PF_KTHREAD | PF_USER_WORKER)); }`, and replaces the previous flag-only checks in `kernel/events/callchain.c` and `kernel/events/core.c` because “checking the flags is still not enough” and “perf would read the mm field it would crash with at NULL pointer dereference.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a helper to पहचानize user tasks by excluding kernel threads and user workers.
intent_record.what: A new static __always_inline helper function `is_user_task(struct task_struct *task)` was added. It returns true when `task->mm` is non-NULL and the task does not have either `PF_KTHREAD` or `PF_USER_WORKER` set in `task->flags`.
intent_record.how: This introduces a reusable predicate for identifying ordinary user tasks, excluding kernel threads and user worker tasks. At runtime, code can now distinguish user-space processes from kernel-owned execution contexts with a single check.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use `is_user_task()` instead of checking specific flags when deciding whether to gather a user callchain from a non-user-mode context.
intent_record.what: In get_perf_callchain(), the condition inside the `if (!user_mode(regs))` branch was changed from checking `current->flags & (PF_KTHREAD | PF_USER_WORKER)` to calling `!is_user_task(current)` before jumping to `exit_put`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the code now uses the helper `is_user_task()` to decide whether the current task can be treated as a user task when collecting a user callchain from kernel mode. This changes which tasks are rejected before `task_pt_regs(current)` is used, aligning the decision with the kernel's broader user-task classification.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use is_user_task() to correctly decide when perf can sample user registers for the current task.
intent_record.what: In perf_sample_regs_user(), the condition guarding the call to perf_get_regs_user() was changed from checking that current does not have PF_KTHREAD or PF_USER_WORKER set to calling is_user_task(current) instead.
intent_record.how: At runtime, user register collection now follows the kernel's user-task classification helper rather than a direct flag exclusion, so perf will only attempt to fetch user regs for tasks considered user tasks by that helper and will skip it for non-user tasks.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use `is_user_task()` to correctly decide when perf can attempt IRQ-safe user page lookup.
intent_record.what: The condition guarding the IRQ-safe get_user_page_fast_only path was changed from `!(current->flags & (PF_KTHREAD | PF_USER_WORKER))` to `is_user_task(current)`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the code now uses the kernel's user-task predicate instead of manually checking two task flags before attempting the fast page lookup. This changes which tasks are allowed to take the user-page resolution path, keeping the logic aligned with the broader definition of a user task and leaving `phys_addr` as 0 when the predicate is false.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the standard user-task check when determining whether perf should collect user callchains.
intent_record.what: The boolean expression initializing `user` in `perf_callchain()` was changed from checking `!(current->flags & (PF_KTHREAD | PF_USER_WORKER))` to calling `is_user_task(current)`.
intent_record.how: This changes the condition used to decide whether user-space callchains may be collected: instead of directly filtering out kernel threads and user workers via task flags, the code now uses the kernel's user-task helper, which may more consistently classify whether the current task should be treated as a user task for callchain collection.

consistency_review.core_intent: Use the standard is_user_task() check in perf to decide when to collect user callchains or sample user-related context.

relevance_review.reason: The change only adds a helper that identifies user tasks by checking PF_KTHREAD/PF_USER_WORKER flags, which is the same flawed criterion described in the root cause. It does not address the missing mm lifetime check or the NULL dereference issue.

The root cause is an incorrect task check in perf that relied on flags instead of a safer user-task predicate, allowing access to freed mm state. This group replaces that logic with is_user_task() in the callchain/register sampling paths, directly addressing the vulnerability.

The change directly addresses the root cause: perf was using an insufficient task-flag check to decide whether user-space state was safe to access, which could lead to dereferencing a freed or NULL mm. Replacing that logic with is_user_task() is the intended fix.

candidates.rationale: This flag check is the unsafe user-task test described in the root cause. A task can have these flags while its mm is already gone during exit, so using it to decide whether it is safe to access user-space state can lead perf to dereference task->mm when it is NULL.

This condition gates access to user registers based only on PF_KTHREAD/PF_USER_WORKER. That is the vulnerable logic because it treats any non-kthread/non-user-worker task as having valid user-space state even if its mm has already been freed.

This expression is the direct user-callchain eligibility check. It incorrectly assumes the presence or absence of these flags is sufficient to determine whether user callchain collection is safe, which can later lead to dereferencing a freed mm.

This is the unsafe guard before attempting IRQ-safe user page lookup. It relies on PF_KTHREAD/PF_USER_WORKER instead of a real user-task/mm validity check, so perf may proceed to user-space memory access after mm teardown.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the unsafe user-task test in the callchain path. It uses only PF_KTHREAD/PF_USER_WORKER to decide whether user-space state is accessible, but those flags can still be set after a task's mm has been freed during exit, leading perf to dereference a NULL task->mm.
This condition gates user-register sampling using only PF_KTHREAD/PF_USER_WORKER. That makes it possible to treat a task as safe for user-space access even when its mm has already been torn down.

This is the unsafe guard before IRQ-safe user page lookup. It relies on the same insufficient flag check instead of verifying that the task still has valid user-space memory, which can lead to access after mm teardown.

This expression directly implements the flawed user-callchain eligibility decision. It assumes the flag state alone is enough to determine whether user callchain collection is safe, which is the root cause.
